chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the killing of the tortoise and the quail: is its meat eaten? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَ يُؤْكَلُ: Is it eaten? (referring to permissibility of consumption)
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ: The tortoise (specifically the land tortoise in this context)
key_terms.وَالْبُنْدُقِ: The quail (a type of small bird)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of tortoise and quail permissible to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the ruling on consuming tortoise and quail, explicitly stating they are not eaten. This reflects the Shia juristic view that distinguishes these creatures from generally permissible game, often linking their status to specific characteristics or prophetic tradition rather than general hunting rules.
